questions.q: NoSQL injection may enable an attacker to do which of the following?
choices: Bypass authentication or protection mechanisms
Extract or edit data
Cause a denial of service
Execute code on the server
Physically damage the database hardware
questions.explain: The topic lists four outcomes: bypassing authentication/protection, extracting or editing data, causing a denial of service, and executing code on the server.

questions.q: NoSQL databases use a single universal standard query language like SQL.
questions.explain: NoSQL databases use a wide range of query languages instead of a universal standard like SQL, and have fewer relational constraints.

questions.q: What is NoSQL injection?
choices: A vulnerability where an attacker can interfere with the queries an application makes to a NoSQL database
A flaw that only affects relational SQL databases
A misconfiguration of TLS certificates on a database server
A technique for encrypting data at rest in NoSQL stores
questions.explain: NoSQL injection is a vulnerability where an attacker is able to interfere with the queries that an application makes to a NoSQL database.

questions.q: What are the two types of NoSQL injection?
choices: Syntax injection and operator injection
Blind injection and error-based injection
In-band injection and out-of-band injection
Stored injection and reflected injection
questions.explain: The two types are syntax injection (breaking the query syntax) and operator injection (using NoSQL query operators to manipulate queries).

questions.q: Which type of NoSQL injection occurs when you can break the NoSQL query syntax to inject your own payload?
choices: Syntax injection
Operator injection
Timing injection
Schema injection
questions.explain: Syntax injection occurs when you can break the NoSQL query syntax, enabling you to inject your own payload; the methodology is similar to SQL injection.

questions.q: Operator injection occurs when you can do what?
choices: Use NoSQL query operators to manipulate queries
Break the string-quoting syntax of the query
Overflow a fixed-length buffer in the driver
Downgrade the database to an older version
questions.explain: Operator injection occurs when you can use NoSQL query operators (such as $ne, $where, $in, $regex) to manipulate queries.

questions.q: How can you potentially detect NoSQL syntax injection vulnerabilities?
choices: By systematically submitting fuzz strings and special characters that trigger a database error or other detectable behavior
By scanning open ports on the database server
By checking the database's TLS certificate expiry
By measuring CPU usage of the web server
questions.explain: You test each input by submitting fuzz strings and special characters that trigger a database error or some other detectable behavior if they aren't adequately sanitized or filtered.

questions.q: To confirm you can influence boolean conditions, you send one request with a false condition and one with a true condition. Which pair does this?
choices: $ne  and  $eq
sleep(5000)  and  sleep(0)
{"$where":"a"}  and  {"$where":"b"}
questions.explain: The conditional statements ' && 0 && 'x (false) and ' && 1 && 'x (true) test whether the false condition impacts query logic, indicating injection affects a server-side query.

questions.q: Which injected JavaScript condition always evaluates to true, letting the modified query return all items (for example turning the query into this.category == 'fizzy'||'1'=='1')?
questions.explain: Injecting '||'1'=='1 produces this.category == 'fizzy'||'1'=='1', which is always true and returns all items including hidden categories.

questions.q: Why might an attacker add a null character after a value, as in category=fizzy'%00?
choices: MongoDB may ignore all characters after a null character, dropping additional conditions like this.released == 1
The null character forces MongoDB to return an error message revealing the schema
It causes the database to switch to SQL mode
It encrypts the rest of the query so the server cannot read it
questions.explain: MongoDB may ignore all characters after a null character, so additional restrictions (e.g. this.released == 1) are removed and unreleased products are displayed too.

questions.q: After submitting ' causes a changed response, how can you confirm it broke the query syntax rather than just changing data?
choices: Submit an escaped quote (e.g. '\'') and check that the syntax error goes away
Submit the same ' character twice more
Switch the request to a GET request
Add a $where operator to the body
questions.explain: Submitting a valid query string such as an escaped quote ('\'') that does not cause a syntax error suggests the application is vulnerable to injection.

questions.q: In MongoDB, what does the $ne operator match?
choices: All values that are not equal to a specified value
Documents that satisfy a JavaScript expression
All values specified in an array
Documents whose values match a regular expression
questions.explain: $ne matches all values that are not equal to a specified value.

questions.q: What does MongoDB's $where operator do?
choices: Matches documents that satisfy a JavaScript expression
Matches all values not equal to a specified value
Matches all values specified in an array
Sorts documents by a given field
questions.explain: $where matches documents that satisfy a JavaScript expression, which is why it can be abused to run limited JavaScript.

questions.q: What does the $in operator match?
choices: All of the values specified in an array
Values not equal to a specified value
Values matching a regular expression
Documents satisfying a JavaScript expression
questions.explain: $in matches all of the values specified in an array, e.g. {"username":{"$in":["admin","administrator","superadmin"]}}.

questions.q: In a JSON message, how do you insert a query operator to turn {"username":"wiener"} into an injection test?
choices: As a nested object, e.g. {"username":{"$ne":"invalid"}}
As an appended string, e.g. {"username":"wiener$ne"}
As a URL parameter, e.g. username[$ne]=invalid
As an HTTP header, e.g. X-Operator: $ne
questions.explain: In JSON messages you insert query operators as nested objects: {"username":"wiener"} becomes {"username":{"$ne":"invalid"}}.

questions.q: If both the username and password inputs process the operator, the payload {"username":{"$ne":"invalid"},"password":{"$ne":"invalid"}} typically logs you in as whom?
choices: The first user in the collection
The administrator by name
A randomly selected user
The most recently created user
questions.explain: The query returns all credentials where both fields are not equal to 'invalid', so you are logged in as the first user in the collection.

questions.q: For URL-based input, how can username=wiener be rewritten to inject the $ne operator?
choices: username[$ne]=invalid
username=$ne:invalid
username={"$ne":"invalid"}
$ne[username]=invalid
questions.explain: For URL-based inputs you insert query operators via URL parameters: username=wiener becomes username[$ne]=invalid. If that fails you can convert the request to a JSON POST.

questions.q: Which MongoDB operator/function can run limited JavaScript, making data exfiltration possible?
choices: $where (and the mapReduce() function)
$in
$ne
$sort
questions.explain: Some operators/functions run limited JavaScript, such as MongoDB's $where operator and mapReduce() function, letting the database evaluate injected JavaScript.

questions.q: What does the injected payload "$where":"Object.keys(this)[0].match('^.{0}a.*')" let you do?
choices: Extract a data field name character by character
Delete the first field of every document
Rename the first field to 'a'
Count the number of documents in the collection
questions.explain: It inspects the first data field in the user object and returns the first character of the field name, enabling extraction of the field name character by character.

questions.q: How can the $regex operator be used even when you cannot run JavaScript, e.g. {"username":"admin","password":{"$regex":"^a.*"}}?
choices: To extract data such as a password character by character
To disable password hashing on the server
To cause a guaranteed 5-second delay
To list all collections in the database
questions.explain: The $regex operator lets you extract data character by character; this example checks whether the password begins with 'a'.

questions.q: When testing whether a 'password' field exists with payloads like admin' && this.password!=' , how do you interpret the responses?
choices: If the field exists, the response matches that of a known existing field and differs from that of a non-existent field
If the field exists, the response is always an error
If the field exists, the response is empty
The response is identical for all fields regardless of existence
questions.explain: You compare against a known existing field (username) and a non-existent one (foo); a matching response for 'password' indicates the field exists.

questions.q: Why might you need to identify valid field names before extracting data from MongoDB via JavaScript injection?
choices: MongoDB handles semi-structured data that doesn't require a fixed schema
MongoDB encrypts all field names by default
MongoDB only allows queries on indexed fields
MongoDB randomizes field names on every query
questions.explain: Because MongoDB handles semi-structured data without a fixed schema, you may need to identify valid fields (by dictionary attack or operator injection) before extracting their values.

questions.q: When is timing-based NoSQL injection useful?
choices: When triggering a database error doesn't cause any difference in the application's response
When the application returns detailed error messages
When the database is a key-value store with no query language
When you already have admin credentials
questions.explain: When an error doesn't change the response, you can still detect/exploit the vulnerability by using JavaScript injection to trigger a conditional time delay.

questions.q: Which payload causes an intentional delay to confirm injection?
choices: {"$where": "sleep(5000)"}
questions.explain: {"$where": "sleep(5000)"} causes an intentional delay of 5000 ms on successful injection; a slower response indicates success.

questions.q: What is the first step when conducting timing-based NoSQL injection?
choices: Load the page several times to determine a baseline loading time
Insert the timing payload immediately
Delete the target user record
Switch the request method to GET
questions.explain: First load the page several times to establish a baseline loading time, then insert a timing-based payload and check whether the response loads more slowly.

questions.q: Which broad guidelines help prevent NoSQL injection?
choices: Sanitize and validate user input using an allowlist of accepted characters
Insert user input using parameterized queries instead of concatenating it directly
Apply an allowlist of accepted keys to prevent operator injection
Concatenate user input directly into queries for performance
questions.explain: Recommended guidelines: allowlist input characters, use parameterized queries rather than concatenation, and allowlist accepted keys to stop operator injection.

questions.q: Which NoSQL database model stores data in flexible, semi-structured documents (formats like JSON, BSON, XML) and includes MongoDB and Couchbase?
choices: Document stores
Key-value stores
Wide-column stores
Graph databases
questions.explain: Document stores keep data in flexible, semi-structured documents (JSON, BSON, XML); examples include MongoDB and Couchbase.

questions.q: Which model stores each data field against a unique key string and includes Redis and Amazon DynamoDB?
choices: Key-value stores
Document stores
Graph databases
Wide-column stores
questions.explain: Key-value stores associate each data field with a unique key; values are retrieved by that key. Examples: Redis and Amazon DynamoDB.

questions.q: Which NoSQL model uses nodes to store data entities and edges to store relationships, with examples Neo4j and Amazon Neptune?
choices: Graph databases
Wide-column stores
Key-value stores
Document stores
questions.explain: Graph databases use nodes for data entities and edges for relationships between them; examples include Neo4j and Amazon Neptune.

questions.q: Apache Cassandra and Apache HBase are examples of which NoSQL model?
choices: Wide-column stores, which organize related data into flexible column families
Document stores, which use JSON/BSON documents
Key-value stores, which use a unique key per value
Graph databases, which use nodes and edges
questions.explain: Wide-column stores organize related data into flexible column families rather than traditional rows; examples include Apache Cassandra and Apache HBase.
